item.title: Pair density waves via interband pairing --- a perspective from superfluid weight
item.description: arXiv:2610.41687v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pair density waves (PDW) are superconducting states that exhibit a spatially modulated pairing order parameter, corresponding to Cooper pairs carrying finite center-of-mass momentum. While some recent studies have emphasized the role of quantum geometry in stabilizing PDW order in certain multiband systems, we here present a systematic investigation of an alternative, geometry-independent mechanism: PDW order driven purely by interband Cooper pairing. Using the superfluid weight (SW) as a diagnostic, we study two canonical models. The first is the classic Fulde-Ferrell model of an $s$-wave superconductor subject to a Zeeman splitting field, which realizes pure interband pairing between two rigidly shifted bands; the second is a spinless honeycomb-lattice model with nearest-neighbor $f$-wave pairing, a modified version of which was recently found to exhibit PDW instability in density-matrix renormalization-group simulations. In both models the SW receives no quantum geometric contribution at the mean-field level, yet it can be greatly suppressed or even turn negative, signaling a tendency toward pairing with spatial phase modulations. For the first model, we establish that the SW is increasingly suppressed as the Zeeman field grows, drastically turning negative upon the emergence of extensive gapless excitations, i.e., the Bogoliubov Fermi surfaces. For the honeycomb $f$-wave model, we demonstrate, both analytically and numerically, vanishing quantum-geometric SW and an invariably negative total SW. Our results thus establish the SW as a qualitative indicator of the tendency toward PDW order, and provide a microscopic rationale for the interband-pairing-driven PDW instability.
item.dc:creator: Yi-Jian Hu, Yi-Fan Jiang, Wen Huang

item.title: Creating functional nanostructures for vortex manipulation in superconducting Bi$_\text{2}$Sr$_\text{2}$CaCu$_\text{2}$O$_\text{8+x}$ thin films via focused He ion beam irradiation
item.description: arXiv:2610.41827v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bi$_2$Sr$_2$CaCu$_2$O$_{8+x}$ (Bi-2212) is a highly anisotropic high-temperature superconductor exhibiting unique vortex dynamics due to its layered structure. Precise nanoscale patterning of ultrathin Bi-2212 films remains challenging, limiting controlled studies of vortex pinning. Here, we employ 30 keV focused helium ion beam (He-FIB) irradiation to fabricate periodic arrays of columnar defects with 100 nm spacings in optimally-doped Bi-2212 thin films, thereby creating artificial vortex pinning centers. Magnetotransport measurements reveal pronounced vortex matching effects, evidenced by minima in magnetoresistance and peaks in critical current at commensurate magnetic fields. The angular dependence of magnetoresistance and critical current scale with an effective magnetic field, indicating strong confinement of pancake vortices along irradiation-induced tracks. These findings demonstrate the efficacy of He-FIB nanopatterning in modulating the superconducting properties in Bi-2212 thin films, providing a platform for fundamental studies of vortex matter and advancing prospects for device applications based on this highly anisotropic superconductor.
item.dc:creator: Bernd Aichner, Christoph Schmid, Sandra Keppert, Reinhold Kleiner, Edward Goldobin, Johannes D. Pedarnig, Dieter Koelle, Wolfgang Lang

item.title: Frustration-Induced $1/6$-Vortex-Paired Phase in a Kagome XY Model
item.description: arXiv:2610.41161v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Geometric frustration can fractionalize vortices in two-dimensional XY systems, but a given frustrated model usually hosts only a single type of fractional vortex. Here we study a kagome XY model in which an antiferromagnetic coupling $J_1$ and a second-harmonic coupling $K$ favor two competing frustrated ground-state manifolds. For $K/J_1<1/9$, the ground states map onto those of the kagome three-state Potts antiferromagnet and support $1/3$ vortices; for $K/J_1>1/9$, they map onto those of the kagome Ising antiferromagnet and support $1/2$ vortices. At $K/J_1=1/9$, the two manifolds become degenerate, and bends in the domain walls between them carry $1/6$-vortex excitations. Tensor-network calculations show that a finite-temperature phase with quasi-long-range order only in $e^{6i\theta}$ emerges from this degenerate point, separating the $1/3$- and $1/2$-vortex-paired phases. This $1/6$-vortex-paired phase has no counterpart in either parent manifold, showing that competing frustrated manifolds provide a route to new fractional-vortex-paired phases.
item.dc:creator: Tong-Yu Lin, Guang-Ming Zhang

item.title: Phase transition dynamics of Abelian-Higgs vortices in the oscillating axion background
item.description: arXiv:2610.41575v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the effect of an oscillating axion background on thermally induced vortex-antivortex production in the Abelian-Higgs model. Through its coupling to the gauge field, the axion sources an electromagnetic response in the presence of vortex magnetic flux, modifying the dynamics of the vortices. We study this system using Langevin lattice simulations with dissipation and stochastic noise. It is shown that the phase transition dynamics of Abelian-Higgs vortices, namely the pair creation of vortex and antivortex under thermal fluctuations, can be significantly modified in the oscillating axion background. We find that the axion background shifts the rapid increase in the vortex density to lower temperature. In particular, this transition temperature becomes smaller as the oscillation frequency of the axion increases. The temperature dependence of the correlation length is also modified. These features provide a new experimental approach for the axion dark matter using superconducting devices.
item.dc:creator: Naoya Kitajima, Shota Nakagawa

item.title: Andreev-Enhanced Conductance in a Bilayer Graphene Quantum Point Contact
item.description: arXiv:2610.41915v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum point contacts provide a platform for probing mode-dependent Andreev reflection. Here, we demonstrate Andreev-enhanced conductance in a gate-defined bilayer graphene quantum point contact coupled to a superconducting aluminum electrode. Electrostatic gating enables sequential mode occupation, verified by normal-state conductance quantization. In the superconducting state, the conductance is enhanced within the conductance plateaus, while the enhancement decreases between plateaus, consistent with the nonlinear transmission dependence of Andreev reflection. The enhancement yields effective transmission probabilities up to 0.9, and extends over a bias window of approximately 140 $\mu$V, which we associate with a proximity-induced superconducting gap, close to the gap of the aluminum film. For in-plane fields, the enhancement persists up to the critical field, and the bias window follows the spectral gap predicted by Abrikosov-Gor'kov theory. In contrast, perpendicular fields suppress the enhancement approximately linearly from zero field, deviating from homogeneous pair breaking and indicative of flux penetration.
item.dc:creator: Emma Horgan, Bernd Aichner, Nadine Omar, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Luca Banszerus

item.title: Superconductivity in doped spin multimer systems
item.description: arXiv:2605.22128v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Binding energy, which quantifies pair formation, is a key factor in the emergence of superconductivity. Here, we show that even when multiple spins are complexly coupled, hole-doped systems can be mapped, in the strong-binding-energy limit, onto an effective hardcore boson model equivalent to the XXZ model, and exhibit promising signatures of superconductivity. We demonstrate this theory analytically and numerically in the double Kondo lattice model. Using the density-matrix renormalization group method, we show that a pairing state is maintained via a crossover even for parameters away from the strong-coupling regime. Additionally, we find that once binding energies are sufficiently generated, pair correlations develop similarly regardless of the details of local spin correlations. Our findings provide useful insights into the mechanism of superconductivity.
item.dc:creator: Ritsuki Hirabayashi, Masataka Kakoi, Ryota Ueda, Kazuhiko Kuroki, Tatsuya Kaneko

item.title: Resonant suppression of the $\pi$-type Josephson component in a Kitaev-ladder junction
item.description: arXiv:2610.23875v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study how discrete normal-segment levels control equilibrium Josephson transport between two Kitaev-ladder superconductors. Away from resonance, detuning opens a selective-clamping window: inter-leg hybridization removes the phase dependence of a $0$-favoring low-energy ground-state contribution while retaining a competing $\pi$-favoring contribution, allowing a smooth negative first harmonic even for bulk-topologically trivial leads. At resonance and $\phi=\pi$, an exact collective-clamping identity makes both low-energy ground-state contributions phase independent above a threshold, although individual quasiparticle levels can remain dispersive. Finite-energy quasiparticles then produce a positive residual first harmonic in a controlled sweet-point regime. For fixed $0<\phi<\pi$, helicity mixing instead yields a positive resonant low-energy harmonic in the weak-coupling limit. Exact identities, fourth-order sign rules, and recursive Green-function calculations establish how resonant alignment changes the spectral contributions governing Josephson phase selection.
item.dc:creator: Cheng-Rong Xie, Hiroki Tsuchiura, Yukio Tanaka

item.title: Chiral Majorana hinge modes on a curved surface with magnetic impurities
item.description: arXiv:2310.09258v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Chiral Majorana modes, a key ingredient for topological quantum computation, arise on the surface of a three-dimensional time-reversal-invariant topological superconductor when a magnetic field induces a sign-changing surface mass. In practice, the orbital response of the superconductor tilts the surface spectrum and overwhelms the Zeeman term as the field grows. Here we show that magnetic impurities on a spherical surface can instead generate this mass term through their exchange coupling, so that only a weak field is required. The Ising surface Majorana modes mediate a ferromagnetic Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yosida (RKKY) interaction, derived here on the curved surface, that orders the radial impurity moments into an inversion-breaking hedgehog at zero field. An axial field instead stabilizes a domain wall across which the radial magnetization reverses sign, leaving a single chiral Majorana mode along the equator and realizing an inversion-protected second-order topological superconductor.
item.dc:creator: Ilyoun Na, James G. McHugh, Sin\'ead M. Griffin, Luca Chirolli

item.title: Quantum Batteries in two-dimensional material-based Josephson Junctions
item.description: arXiv:2605.22582v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate the solid-state implementation of a Dicke-like quantum battery consisting of a two-dimensional material-based Josephson junction inductively coupled to a resonator, using graphene as a representative example. In this configuration, Andreev bound states naturally act as non-interacting, energetically non-degenerate two-level systems, and the setup allows for both single-photon and two-photon resonant processes. The coupling between the LC-circuit flux and the supercurrent through the junction gives rise to peculiar longitudinal interaction terms that have no counterpart in the conventional Dicke model. We demonstrate that these additional couplings can enhance energy storage for a proper range of parameters. The proposed architecture also enables an alternative, but comparable, charging protocol that relies on tuning the superconducting phase difference across the junction.
item.dc:creator: V. Varrica, G. Gemme, F. M. D. Pellegrino, E. Paladino, M. Sassetti, D. Ferraro
